Division by E R² and k+1~r_k²γ yields the stated sharp coefficient, with uniform error. The periodic phase map D_g is strictly increasing, and constant phase coefficient forces g′/g constant hence g constant.

value.rationale: Radial Toeplitz algebras are represented by moment eigenvalue sequences and the square-root metric controls their continuity. The exact norm of each adjacent coordinate difference is an intrinsic operator-theoretic local sensitivity, not an arbitrary selected parameter. The theorem identifies exact finite-k optimizer, sharp high-frequency local Lipschitz constant and a complete geometric transition: even with uniformly convex smooth curvature, the optimal local sensitivity detects g′/g and has a nontrivial periodic interval of cluster values. It answers a quantitatively natural question left by eigenvalue representation and metric regularity results.
